newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.5/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.5/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.5/11.0 percent on Thursday morning on sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said an early central bank supply of 363 billion rupiah and a stabilised money market late on Wednesday seemed to calm overall market sentiment.
Short-term swaps also softened on steady liquidity.
One-week money was traded at 11.50/11.75 and one-month rates were at 12.75/12.875 percent.
One local bank dealer said operators remained cautious about short-term liquidity in the run-up to the end of the month because of possible window-dressing at the half-yearly book closing.
"People might need more rupiah at book closing on June 30. We remain cautious," the dealer said.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 14.16 percent against 16.12 percent on Tuesday.
